name: Kadi Pakora
ingredients: Mustard oil for frying and tempering
instructions: 1. Whisk curd, besan, turmeric, and chili powder with water to create a smooth batter.
2. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin and hing, then pour in the batter, stirring continuously until it thickens.
3. Prepare pakoras by mixing sliced onions, besan, salt, and spices with minimal water and deep-frying until golden brown.
4. Drop the fried pakoras into the simmering kadi and let them cook for 10 minutes.
5. Prepare a tadka by heating mustard oil, adding mustard seeds, dried red chilies, and curry leaves.
6. Pour the sizzling tadka over the kadi, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot with steamed rice or bajra roti.
description: Kadi Pakora is a quintessential comfort food in Haryana, deeply rooted in the agricultural lifestyle of the state. It is traditionally prepared using homemade sour curd and fresh gram flour, often served with bajra (pearl millet) roti, reflecting the rustic and wholesome culinary heritage of Haryanvi households.
